title: Proxmox cluster loses quorum after every power cut
author: nas_gardener
body: I run three NUCs in a Proxmox cluster and each time the power drops, two of them come back before the third and the cluster sits there without quorum until I log in and restart corosync by hand. Is there a sane way to make the nodes wait for each other, or should I just add a QDevice on the Raspberry Pi that is always on?

title: ZFS scrub taking 31 hours on 4x12TB raidz1, is that normal?
author: blockpointer
body: The pool is about 70 percent full and the scrub that used to finish overnight now runs for more than a day. SMART looks clean on all four drives. I noticed one disk reports much lower throughput in zpool iostat, so I am starting to suspect a bad SATA cable rather than the drive itself. What would you check first?

title: Finally got 10GbE working over the old Cat5e in my walls
author: copper_optimist
body: Everyone told me I would need to pull new cable, but two runs of roughly 18 metres negotiated at 10G without errors after I re-terminated the keystones. The third run only holds 2.5G. Posting the iperf numbers in case it helps someone decide whether to try before tearing the walls open.

title: Which UPS do you trust for a small rack?
author: voltdrop
body: My load is around 280 watts: a NAS, a switch, the router and one mini PC. I want at least fifteen minutes of runtime and a clean shutdown signal over USB that NUT understands. The APC units are easy to find here but the replacement batteries cost almost as much as the UPS. Any recommendations from people who have run one for a few years?

title: Pi-hole or AdGuard Home in 2026?
author: dnsdave
body: I have used Pi-hole since version 4 and it has been solid, but I keep reading that AdGuard Home handles encrypted upstreams and per-client rules without extra containers. For those who switched, was the migration of blocklists and local DNS records painful, and do you miss anything?

title: Jellyfin hardware transcoding on an N100: my settings
author: quietfan
body: After a weekend of trial and error the box now handles three 4K HDR to 1080p transcodes at once. The things that mattered were passing /dev/dri into the container, enabling low power encoding, and turning tone mapping to the VPP variant. CPU sits under 30 percent. Full compose file is in the reply below.

title: Is it crazy to run the router as a VM?
author: bridgemode
body: I virtualised OPNsense on the same host as everything else to save power. It works well until I need to reboot the hypervisor, at which point the whole house loses internet and my family notices immediately. Thinking about moving it back to a dedicated fanless box. How do the rest of you handle maintenance windows?

title: Backups: restic to Backblaze B2 costs after one year
author: threetwoone
body: A year ago I asked here whether B2 was affordable for about 900 GB of photos and documents. The total for twelve months came to a little under 70 dollars including one full test restore. Pruning weekly keeps the repository from growing. Sharing the numbers because I could not find real figures when I was deciding.

title: Docker containers cannot reach the LAN after enabling IPv6
author: slash64
body: As soon as I set ipv6 to true in daemon.json, containers on the default bridge lost access to anything on 192.168.1.0/24, while the internet still worked. Removing the setting fixes it. I assume it is a forwarding or firewall rule that Docker rewrites, but I cannot see which one. Has anyone traced this?

title: Moving from Nextcloud to plain Syncthing plus Immich
author: selfhostsam
body: Nextcloud did everything but I only ever used file sync and photo upload, and every major upgrade cost me an evening. I split it into Syncthing for documents and Immich for photos three months ago. Fewer features, far less maintenance, and the phone battery lasts longer. Happy to answer questions about the migration.

title: Noisy 40mm fans in a Brocade ICX6450: replacement options
author: rackrash
body: The switch is great for the price but it screams. I measured 58 dB at one metre. I have seen people fit Noctua fans with a resistor so the switch does not report a fan failure. Does anyone have the exact resistor value, and did the temperatures stay acceptable under PoE load?

title: Home Assistant on a VM versus a dedicated Pi
author: zigbee_zoe
body: My Pi 4 with an SD card died for the second time, so I moved Home Assistant OS into a VM and passed the Zigbee dongle through. Restarts are quicker and snapshots before updates have already saved me once. The only downside so far is that the USB passthrough needed a udev rule to survive host reboots.

title: Tailscale exit node is slow, direct connection never established
author: derp_relay
body: From my phone on mobile data the connection to my exit node at home always goes through a relay and tops out around 8 Mbit. The router is behind CGNAT from my ISP. I opened UDP 41641 anyway, with no change. Is there anything left to try short of renting a small VPS as a relay of my own?

title: What is everyone using for secrets in docker compose?
author: envfile
body: Right now my passwords live in .env files next to each compose file, which means they also sit in my backup in plain text. I looked at Docker secrets, SOPS with age, and Vault, and Vault feels like far too much for a single host. Curious what small setups actually settle on.

title: Ceph on three mini PCs with one NVMe each: a cautionary tale
author: placementgroup
body: It worked for six months and performance was fine for VMs. Then one consumer NVMe wore out and during the rebalance a second one started throwing errors. I did not lose data, but only because the backups were current. Consumer drives without power loss protection are simply not made for Ceph's write pattern.

title: Reverse proxy: Caddy made me delete 200 lines of nginx config
author: tls_tom
body: I put off switching for years because the nginx setup worked. Last week I rewrote it in Caddy and the whole file is 40 lines, with certificates handled automatically including the wildcard through DNS challenge. The one thing I had to look up was how to pass the real client IP to the apps behind it.

title: Power draw of an idle Dell R730 versus two mini PCs
author: wattwatcher
body: I measured at the wall for a week each. The R730 with two CPUs and eight drives idles at 142 watts. The pair of mini PCs running the same VMs idles at 23 watts combined. At my electricity price the difference pays for the mini PCs in about fourteen months, and the office is quiet now.

title: Unifi controller in a container keeps losing adoption
author: apmesh
body: Every time the container is recreated, the access points show as disconnected until I SSH into each one and run set-inform again. The inform host override is set to the host IP. I suspect the container is advertising its internal address somewhere. Where does the controller store that?

title: Paperless-ngx: scanner to archive workflow that finally works
author: duplexdan
body: The scanner now sends PDFs to an SMB share, paperless consumes them, runs OCR in German and English, and a few matching rules assign correspondents and tags. Two hundred documents in, I have corrected maybe ten by hand. The trick was scanning at 300 dpi; at 200 the OCR missed too many account numbers.

title: TrueNAS Scale upgrade broke my apps, how do I roll back?
author: bootenv
body: After upgrading to the newest release, none of the apps start and the pool for them shows as not configured. I still have the previous boot environment. Is it safe to activate it and reboot, or will the app datasets already have been migrated in a way the older version cannot read?

title: Monitoring: is Prometheus plus Grafana overkill for four machines?
author: scrape_interval
body: I set up the full stack and it is lovely, but it uses more memory than two of the services it monitors. All I really look at is disk space, temperatures and whether backups ran. Tempted to replace it with something tiny that just sends me a message when a check fails. What do people with small setups use?

title: Label printer recommendations for cables and drives
author: heatshrink
body: My current labels peel off anything warm within a few months. I am looking for a printer that takes laminated tape and can do the wrap-around style for patch cables. Budget is modest and I would rather not be locked into a phone app that needs an account.

title: VLAN for IoT devices: casting stops working across subnets
author: mdns_reflector
body: I moved the TV and speakers to their own VLAN and now phones on the main network cannot find them. I enabled the mDNS repeater on the router and allowed the established traffic back, and discovery works for a minute after boot and then stops. Is there a known firewall rule set that makes this reliable?

title: One year with a used Optiplex as my only server: review
author: sff_fan
body: Bought for 110 euros with an i5-8500 and 16 GB, later upgraded to 32. It runs fourteen containers and two VMs, draws 11 watts idle, and has not crashed once. The only real limit is two drive bays. If you are starting out, I would pick something like this over a Raspberry Pi every time.
